solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Muscle in play, full range

indicators.note: one thing sitting in another means its letters go inside that other word

parts.note: to strum is to play a guitar casually
short for pectoral, a chest muscle

explanation.surface: A sporting or theatrical piece in which some muscle is fully stretched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play' looks like a noun for a drama, but it is the verb for running fingers across guitar strings.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectrum is the complete span of something, as in the whole spectrum of opinion.

clue.text: Friend, mine, took pound

parts.note: a pal is a friend
a pit is a mine, as in a coal pit
ate means took food

explanation.surface: A friend from the mine who took a pound coin, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pound' looks like money but is the verb for a racing heart.
explanation.definitionFit: A heart that palpitates beats fast and hard, which is what a pounding heart does.

clue.text: Noble record

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a European nobleman equal to an earl
second meaning: a tally or reckoning of numbers

explanation.walkthrough: The two words read like praise for an achievement; they are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a continental aristocrat and a recorded tally, such as a vote count.

clue.text: Reason a relation relocated

indicators.note: something relocated has been moved about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters used as written

explanation.surface: Explaining why a family member moved house.
explanation.definitionFit: A rationale is the underlying reason or logic behind a course of action.

clue.text: Knotty art, yours truly entertaining a crowd

indicators.note: to entertain guests is to have them inside your home, so one word holds the other

parts.note: the setter referring to themself
taken as written
to crowd and to cram both mean to pack tightly

explanation.surface: An artist whose intricate work is shown off to a crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knotty' suggests difficult or puzzling, but here it is literal: the art is made of knots.
explanation.definitionFit: Macramé is the craft of tying cord into decorative knots, so it is literally an art of knots.

clue.text: See where there's an absence of rocks?

parts.note: absence expressed as the negative
a drink on the rocks is served over ice

explanation.surface: A puzzled look at a place with no rocks in it.
explanation.walkthrough: Read cryptically, a place with no rocks is NOT ICE.
explanation.definitionFit: To notice something is to see or spot it.

clue.text: A little man as tyrant, odious

indicators.note: only a small part of the following words is taken, a run of letters inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word, the whole second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A small man acting the tyrant is detestable.
explanation.definitionFit: Nasty and odious are synonyms, both meaning thoroughly unpleasant.

clue.text: Time clue about daughter moderated

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round another

parts.note: a crossword clue can be referred to by its number and direction
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A crossword setter softening a clue to help the daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: A crossword clue is named by its number and direction, so 'clue' is a self-referential nod to the solver's own grid; the D goes between its two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Something toned down has been made milder or less extreme, which is to say moderated.

clue.text: City similarly viewed from north and south?

definitions.note: a noun used as a modifier, as in City hall, standing for an adjective

indicators.text: similarly viewed from north and south
indicators.note: in a down entry, reading from the top or from the bottom gives the same letters

parts.note: the word for belonging to a city

explanation.surface: A town that looks the same from either direction of approach.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down light, north and south are top and bottom, and this word reads the same both ways.
explanation.definitionFit: Civic means relating to a city or town, as in civic pride.

clue.text: Number of the French in lacklustre parade

indicators.note: one word placed in another means its letters go inside

parts.note: flat means dull and lifeless
un is French for one

explanation.surface: A French head count at a dull procession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parade' is the verb, to show off, not the procession the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: To flaunt something is to show it off ostentatiously, to parade it.

clue.text: South Africa certainly not toured by wine lover from Italy

indicators.note: a place toured is gone around, so the outer word surrounds it

parts.note: cava is Spanish sparkling wine
standard abbreviation for the country
an emphatic refusal

explanation.surface: A wine tour of South Africa that definitely did not happen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wine lover' looks like one phrase, but the definition begins at 'lover'; cava is Spanish sparkling wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Giacomo Casanova was an eighteenth-century Venetian whose name became a byword for a seducer.

clue.text: Reference to dairy in cream, primarily whipped

indicators.note: whipping cream beats it about, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: the letters used as written

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter is wanted

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A cookery note pointing to the dairy section about whipped cream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reference' looks like part of the surface's 'reference to', but it alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A dictionary is a standard reference book, consulted for word meanings.

clue.text: Watch out for meat!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the shouted warning to lower your head
second meaning: the flesh of a waterbird eaten as food

explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a warning to a vegetarian; the shouted imperative is a separate sense from the poultry.
explanation.definitionFit: Shouting the word warns someone to stoop out of harm's way, and it is also a bird served as roast meat.

clue.text: Repeated phrases with skill recalled by geezer

definitions.note: plural, while the answer is singular

parts.note: geezer is British slang for a man

indicators.note: recalled read as called back, so the word runs in the opposite direction

parts.note: art means skill, as in the art of conversation

explanation.surface: An old chap skilfully remembering catchphrases.
explanation.definitionFit: A mantra is a word or phrase chanted over and over, in meditation or as a slogan.

clue.text: Early riser, one in bed after game of cricket

indicators.note: after says the bed piece is placed second, behind the cricket piece

parts.note: a Test is an international cricket match

indicators.note: one thing in another has its letters placed inside it

parts.note: a garden bed is a plot
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone who gets up early, still in bed after watching cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a joke: such a pilot is among the first to rise in a new aircraft. A Test is an international cricket match.
explanation.definitionFit: A test pilot flies new aircraft before anyone else, so is first into the air, a playful early riser.

clue.text: Tramp embraced by old partners goes off

indicators.note: something embraced is held inside arms, so the outer word surrounds it

parts.note: exes are former spouses or partners
to tramp is to walk heavily, to plod

explanation.surface: A vagrant welcomed by former partners who then leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tramp' reads as a homeless person but is the verb, to walk heavily.
explanation.definitionFit: A bomb that explodes goes off, the phrasal verb for detonating.

clue.text: Cat has paw in hedge

parts.note: pussy is a familiar word for a cat
an animal's paw is its foot

explanation.surface: A cat with one paw stuck in a hedgerow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hedge' is the verb for avoiding commitment, not the garden bush.
explanation.definitionFit: To pussyfoot is to act cautiously and avoid committing oneself, which is to hedge.

clue.text: Serenity affected fielding a viewer's complaint

indicators.note: a fielder takes in the ball, so the reworked word holds the next piece
something affected has been altered, so its letters change order

parts.note: the letters used as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Calm disrupted while fielding, as a cricketer squints into the sun.
explanation.walkthrough: SERENITY rearranged gives EYESTRIN, which then takes A between R and I.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyestrain is tiredness of the eyes, a common complaint of anyone who watches screens for long.

clue.text: Ma has resewn faulty trousers, say

indicators.note: faulty work is botched, so the letters come out in the wrong order

parts.note: the letters used as written
the letters used as written

explanation.surface: Mum has stitched up some trousers again, badly.
explanation.definitionFit: Menswear is clothing for men, and trousers are one example, as 'say' signals.

clue.text: Agitated bird shown the way

parts.note: a ruff is a wading bird
led means guided, shown the way

explanation.surface: A distressed bird being guided along a path.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruffled means upset or disturbed, as in ruffled feathers, so it is a synonym for agitated.

clue.text: Fourteen lines: four fewer and numbers reversed

indicators.note: the joined pieces are turned around and read from end to start

parts.note: four fewer than the fourteen just named
the usual abbreviation for numbers

explanation.surface: Instructions for trimming a poem: cut four lines and turn the numbering round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'four fewer' leans on the definition: fourteen minus four is TEN. TEN NOS is then read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A sonnet is a poem of exactly fourteen lines, as in Shakespeare's and Petrarch's.

clue.text: Rugby player has run in try

indicators.note: one thing in another has its letters placed inside it

parts.note: to have a pop at something is to try it
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A rugby player running in to score a try.
explanation.walkthrough: 'try' is not the rugby score but an attempt, a pop; R goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A prop is a forward in the front row of a rugby scrum.

clue.text: Old magistrate looking at first lady

parts.note: re means regarding, concerning
in Genesis, Eve was the first woman

explanation.surface: A judge of former times eyeing the president's wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first lady' suggests a president's wife; here it is the biblical Eve.
explanation.definitionFit: A reeve was a local official in medieval England with powers like a magistrate's.

clue.text: L-L-luck of the draw?

wordplay.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty, and there are two of them

explanation.surface: A stammered remark about chance outcomes.
explanation.walkthrough: The stutter is not decoration: its two letters L stand for two fifties.
explanation.definitionFit: A fifty-fifty outcome is an even chance, where the result is down to luck.

clue.text: Quick craft

definitions.note: plural sense: a number of vessels
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a group of ships or vessels

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a speedy boat; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an adjective for swift movement and a noun for a body of ships or boats sailing together.

clue.text: Optimal reports looked at fish?

indicators.note: a report is spoken account, so the sound of the words matters, not their spelling

parts.note: eyed means looked at, and an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: A question about whether the best accounts studied fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideal and optimal both mean the best possible.

clue.text: My my, two deep holes!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an exclamation of surprise
second meaning: a pair of shafts sunk for water

explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation reads as a reaction to the holes, but it is a definition in its own right.
explanation.definitionFit: The doubled word is an expression of mild surprise and also, literally, a shaft sunk for water named twice.

clue.text: Nothing original, certainly, describing some streets

parts.note: zero, shaped like O
original means new, never done before
ay is an old or dialect yes

explanation.surface: Remarking that there is nothing original in the look of certain roads.
explanation.definitionFit: One-way is the label for streets where traffic may move in only a single direction.

clue.text: Impersonate a bird and go jump in the lake

parts.note: to be someone on stage is to play or impersonate them
taken as written
a tit is a small songbird

explanation.surface: Telling someone to mimic a bird and then get lost.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as BE A TIT the wordplay also hints at British slang for a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Beat it and go jump in the lake are both rude ways of telling someone to go away.

clue.text: Details accompanying story, tale I end unexpectedly

indicators.note: an unexpected outcome is out of the usual order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters used as written

explanation.surface: A writer finishing a tale with a twist, with notes attached.
explanation.definitionFit: A dateline is the line at the head of a news report giving where and when it was filed.
